tagline: Hand over a stream of small fixes and watch each one ship
use_when: You have a pile of small bugs or requests to report one at a time, often from your phone, and want each one built and merged without being asked questions mid-stream.
try_it: Start a review cycle. First item: the header overlaps the logo on my phone.

features.label: Hand It Over, Walk Away
features.sub: Send reports one at a time or in a batch
features.title: Send reports one at a time or in a batch
features.what: Every message after you open the session is treated as a new item in the queue. Anything you send while an item is in progress waits its turn, so new reports never derail half-finished work.
features.html:
header overlaps the logo on my phone
add a sort-by-date option

features.label: Screenshots On by Default
features.sub: One line tells you screenshots are on; you can opt out
features.title: One line tells you screenshots are on; you can opt out
features.what: The session starts capturing screenshots of every visible fix without asking you a question first. A single line says so, and one reply turns them off for the rest of the session.
features.html:
Screenshots ON. Tell me if you want them OFF.

features.label: A Live Page From Item One
features.sub: A tracking page goes up before the first fix ships
features.title: A tracking page goes up before the first fix ships
features.what: As soon as the first items arrive, a review page is published with one card per item. The same page is updated after every item, so you can follow along at one link instead of waiting for a summary at the end.

features.label: The Before, Caught in Time
features.sub: Claude takes its own before shot when an item comes in
features.title: Claude takes its own before shot when an item comes in
features.what: The before screenshot is captured the moment an item arrives, before any code changes, at both phone and desktop size. Once the fix is in, the old state is gone, so every item you review has something real to compare against.

features.label: No “Go” Needed
features.sub: Moves to the next item on its own, every time
features.title: Moves to the next item on its own, every time
features.what: When one item is done, the next one starts in the same turn. You never have to type continue, and a long turn is not treated as a reason to stop. It only pauses when the queue is empty, everything left is waiting on you, or something destructive needs your OK.

features.label: Test First, Every Fix
features.sub: Each fix starts with a failing test
features.title: Each fix starts with a failing test
features.what: Every change is built test-first, the test suite is run until it is green, and the diff is reviewed before it is committed. A fast loop does not mean a sloppy one.
features.html:
test: header fitsFAILfix → PASS
test written first suite green diff reviewed

features.label: One Fix, One Pull Request
features.sub: Every item gets its own pull request, merged as it goes
features.title: Every item gets its own pull request, merged as it goes
features.what: Each fix lands on its own branch, cut fresh from the main branch, and its pull request is opened and merged in the same turn. Two items share a pull request only when they touch the same code, so any single fix can be found, reviewed or undone on its own. If your project requires a human review on every pull request, say so at the start and the fixes land as open pull requests instead.

features.label: Every Request Finds Its Lane
features.sub: Each item is triaged before anything is built
features.title: Each item is triaged before anything is built
features.what: Small bugs and big feature ideas can arrive in the same stream. Each one is sorted into a lane first: a fix to build now, a design call, a page that looks wrong, a copy edit, a photo, a style rule, a feature to save for later, or a question only you can answer.

features.label: Design Reviews Start Themselves
features.sub: A taste call gets its own design review, unasked
features.title: A taste call gets its own design review, unasked
features.what: When an item has more than one good answer, the design-review skill runs for it on its own: a before screenshot, real mockups, a page to pick from. A page that looks wrong gets visual-qa, copy gets article-copy-edit, a missing picture gets photo-picker. You never have to ask for one, and the queue keeps moving while you decide.

features.label: Big Ideas Become To-dos
features.sub: A real feature is saved, not half-built
features.title: A real feature is saved, not half-built
features.what: A request that needs its own plan is saved to your to-do list in your words, with a one-line scope and its open questions, instead of being started inside a session of quick fixes.

features.label: Hard Bugs Still Get Fixed
features.sub: A tricky bug is debugged, not handed back
features.title: A tricky bug is debugged, not handed back
features.what: Being hard to track down is not a reason to flag a bug. It gets investigated and fixed without you, and only a specific fact or decision that only you have is saved as a question.

features.label: A Line Per Item
features.sub: A short progress line after every item
features.title: A short progress line after every item
features.what: After each item you get one line: what it was, whether it shipped, went to a design review, was saved as a to-do or was flagged, and how many are left. It is there for you to glance at and needs no reply.

features.what: Each item gets an entry in the project's to-do file with what was asked, why it happened, the approach and any assumption made in place of asking. Shipped items are checked off, so nothing ships silently.

features.label: Redirect It Before It’s Built

features.title: Every card has a status and a note box
features.what: Each card shows where it stands: Reported, In progress, Shipped, In design review, Saved as a to-do or Flagged. A note box is there from the start, so you can add detail, change the request or drop it before any work begins.

features.title: Solo work first, then your questions in one batch

features.what: Each shipped card offers Looks right, Comment, Request revision and Revert it. Nothing is picked for you, so a fix you never looked at reads as not yet reviewed rather than approved.

features.label: Every Flag Has a Next Step
features.sub: Flagged items say where they go from here
features.title: Flagged items say where they go from here
features.what: Each flagged item lists why it was held back and the next step, such as a design review, a planning session or simply your decision. A chat recap lists what shipped, what was flagged and anything left half done.

features.label: Save Points
features.sub: Long sessions save their progress between items
features.title: Long sessions save their progress between items
features.what: A long session saves its progress at an item boundary when a big item finishes and the next is unrelated, after five shipped items, when its memory is half used, or before a clearly large item. Nothing is ever saved mid-item.

features.what: Before saving, it confirms every merge really landed and the tests pass. The handoff note lists the whole queue, what is merged, what is still open, decisions made, and anything you said that nobody has acted on yet.

features.what: A save point is announced in one line and the next item starts right away; you are never asked to restart the session. If you do clear it, the next session picks up from the handoff note without re-reading old work.
